candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22. With the launch, it says it raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.

A usage limit is the amount a plan lets you use within a stated time window. A higher limit may mean more use before you have to wait for the five-hour allowance to reset. Anthropic does not say how much more or promise a message count.
Anthropic also says subscription users get a rate-limit reset they can save and use when they choose.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: In addition to the price drop, we’re increasing five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. We’re also providing subscription users a rate limit reset, which you can now save and use whenever you choose.

scopeAndFreshness: P002 and P004 match the source's 'increasing five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans' and the saveable rate-limit reset; P003 correctly notes the source gives no increase size or message count.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Opus 5.5 is particularly good at long and sprawling jobs like codebase-wide migrations and audits.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Compared with Fable 5.1, Anthropic says Opus 5.5 performs similarly on most work. That does not show Opus 5.5 is necessary for a routine email or summary; another Claude model may be enough. Anthropic’s performance, speed, safety and cost-per-task claims are not independently validated here.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: We’re introducing Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in our new Claude 5.5 family. It performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5.

scopeAndFreshness: P008 matches the source's 'performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work,' keeps attribution, and correctly adds that provider claims are not independently validated here.
